summary: Burst of 5xx errors traced to connection churn causing upstream runtime restarts and proxy fanout failures
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses for a single dedicated customer (CanopyHealth). Impact: customer traffic experienced ~18% 5xx rate for ~90 minutes, causing degraded UX for their production feature. Environment: prod us-east-1, Dedicated pool for CanopyHealth. Observed behavior: API gateway returned 502/503/504 and occasionally 500. Upstream serving-runtime instances intermittently exited and were restarted by the node agent. We saw increased connection churn from the tenant which coincided with the surge. Example request IDs: req_8a2f1b, req_8a2f2c, req_8a2f3e. Incident triage kicked off in #support and #incidents-channel.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic pattern: many short-lived connections with small payloads (~100-200 tokens).
2) Simulate burst of concurrent connections (500-800 concurrent TLS handshakes) against tenant endpoint in us-east-1.
3) Observe API gateway metrics: connection opens/closes, queue length, and 5xx rate.
4) Observe serving-runtime pods for OOMs, segfaults, or high open file descriptors.

investigation_notes: 14:20 UTC: API gateway graph shows open_connections spike from 50->900 for tenant CanopyHealth over ~2 minutes.
14:22 UTC: Connection churn correlated with a backlog of TCP sockets in TIME_WAIT and elevated ephemeral port usage on apigw nodes.

14:25 UTC: Serving-runtime metrics show steady memory increase per request; a small subset of requests had unusually large attention windows (customer prompt size + embeddings) causing higher KV cache usage.
14:30 UTC: Autoscaler recently had a config change (PR 2101) that reduced max surge buffer; under this pattern autoscaler failed to pre-warm enough runtimes leading to amplified queueing on apigw.

Hypothesis: Rapid short-lived connections increased file descriptor and socket pressure on apigw. That created a tight fanout to a small number of runtimes; one or two runtimes hit memory limits and were OOM-killed, which caused apigw to report upstream unhealthy and return 5xxs.
comments: Priya Nanduri (Support) 2026-03-10 14:40: Logged initial customer impact and added CanopyHealth contact. Notified SRE on-call.
Lena Weiss (SRE) 2026-03-10 14:48: Observed fd usage at 96% on apigw-12. Increasing ulimit allowed short-term recovery. Opening incident bridge.
Samir Patel (Infra) 2026-03-10 15:05: Rolled back autoscaler config from PR 2101 to restore previous surge capacity. Monitoring for reduction in queueing.
Marta Alvarez (Eng) 2026-03-10 15:40: Deployed runtime patch (PR 4123) that fixes a memory growth path in the quantized attention kernel under specific prompt shapes.
CanopyHealth (Customer) 2026-03-10 16:00: Reported partial recovery; still seeing occasional 5xxs for longer prompts. Provided sample payloads.
Samir Patel (Infra) 2026-03-10 17:10: Increased apigw file descriptor limit and tuned ephemeral port reuse; 5xx rate returned to baseline by 17:05 UTC. Proceeding to postmortem.
Priya Nanduri (Support) 2026-03-12 09:22: Notified customer with root cause summary and remediation steps; ticket awaiting closure after follow-ups.
resolution: Mitigated: rolled back autoscaler surge reduction, increased apigw FD limits, deployed runtime memory-fix patch. 5xx rates returned to baseline and customer traffic normalized. Customer notified and monitoring continues.
root_cause: Interplay of dramatic short-lived connection churn from tenant traffic, reduced autoscaler surge capacity, and a memory growth bug in the quantized attention kernel. Connection pressure concentrated load on a small runtime pool leading to OOM restarts; API gateway reported upstream unhealthy and returned 5xxs.
actions_taken: Rolled back autoscaler PR that reduced surge buffer (apigw/autoscaler config revert).
Temporarily increased file descriptor limits and ephemeral port tuning on apigw nodes.
Deployed serving-runtime patch addressing memory growth in quantized attention (PR 4123).
Notified customer and provided sample mitigations for traffic shaping on their side.
follow_up_items: Add pod-level guardrails to prevent a few runtimes from receiving disproportionate fanout when connection churn is high.
Add alerting for apigw fd usage and ephemeral port exhaustion (thresholds: >=85%).
Hardening: add a circuit-breaker on apigw that prefers spreading connections across more runtime instances earlier.
Run a chaos test simulating tenant short-lived-connection bursts to validate autoscaler and runtime behavior.
